candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Determine a least common denominator and rewrite unlike-denominator fractions or fraction parts as equivalent fractions before subtracting.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S01, B.S01, and C.S01 all describe the same preparatory operation: finding an LCD/common denominator and converting to equivalent fractions before subtraction.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite a whole number or mixed number into a subtraction-ready whole-and-fraction form, such as adding a zero-fraction part, converting a nonstandard mixed number, or decomposing into whole and fractional parts.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S02, B.S02, and C.S02 all cover preparatory rewriting of operands into compatible forms; B and C explicitly include decomposition into whole and fraction parts, which is consistent with A's normalization intent.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract fractions with a common denominator by subtracting numerators, including the fractional parts of mixed numbers after setup is complete.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S03 isolates subtraction of same-denominator fractions or mixed-number fraction parts. In B and C this operation is bundled together with whole-part subtraction inside a broader combined skill rather than separated.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract the whole-number components in a mixed-number or whole-number subtraction once the operands are in compatible form.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S04 isolates subtraction of whole-number components. B.S03 and C.S03 include this operation but combine it with fraction-part subtraction, so they are not exact standalone matches.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract the whole-number parts and/or same-denominator fraction parts separately once the operands are in compatible form.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: B.S03 and C.S03 are direct matches: both combine subtraction of whole parts and aligned fraction parts into one broader computation skill. A splits this concept into two separate skills (A.S03 and A.S04), so no exact single-skill counterpart exists in A.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Regroup by taking 1 from the whole-number part and converting it to fractional units when the minuend’s fraction part is too small to subtract.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S05, B.S04, and C.S04 all describe the same regrouping/borrowing process of converting one whole into n/n to enable fraction subtraction.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce the resulting fraction to lowest terms or rewrite a zero-fraction or whole-valued result in its simplest form.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S06, B.S05, and C.S05 all cover post-subtraction simplification, including fraction reduction and simplifying zero-fraction results to whole numbers or integers.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Assemble the computed whole-number and fractional parts into the final mixed number, fraction, or integer answer.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S07, B.S06, and C.S06 all describe recombining computed parts into the final presented answer; naming differs slightly but the cognitive concept is the same.

alignment_summary: The three codebooks show strong agreement on most major skills: finding common denominators, normalizing operand form, borrowing/regrouping, simplifying, and composing the final answer all align cleanly across A, B, and C. The main structural difference is that Expert A splits subtraction into two finer-grained skills—subtracting fraction parts and subtracting whole parts—while Experts B and C combine these into a single broader skill, producing one 2/3 alignment plus two A-only 1/3 concepts. All skill IDs from all three experts are mapped exactly once.
